name: Beauty Kernel
intent: Package MOOR's procedural definition of beauty as a reusable grammar: geometric ratios, hierarchy, scale bands, distributions, symmetry/asymmetry, rhythm, color/value hierarchy, edge density, curvature continuity, occlusion, material causality, motion hierarchy, temporal distributions, deterministic variation, restraint, and an exception budget. The kernel must generate deterministic domain-specific beauty contracts without collapsing beauty into a scalar score, and must hand final perceptual judgment to the Convergence Funnel.
composition: GRAMMAR + DOMAIN ADAPTER + DETERMINISTIC CONTRACT COMPILER + CONVERGENCE HANDOFF
rules: Priors are useful ranges, not universal laws.
Use a small shared proportion language instead of arbitrary dimensions.
Use dominant/support/accent hierarchy instead of equal visual weight.
Use macro/meso/micro/temporal bands with meaningful scale separation.
Use causal distributions instead of uniform random scatter.
Use global balance plus local asymmetry and a bounded exception budget.
Preserve quiet regions and information-density rhythm.
Saturation and emissive area become sparser as salience increases.
Occlusion should create depth without destroying silhouette.
Material wear, dirt, wetness, and roughness must have causes.
Motion must inherit from shared causes before local noise.
Randomness must be deterministic and scoped.
Beauty Kernel output constrains generation; it never substitutes for perceptual consequence verification.

integration.reverse: feed the actual result plus the Beauty Contract into the Convergence Funnel
integration.promotion: only after consequence-level comparison reports no material difference
